metaTitle: Pressure Washing Marketing for Exterior Cleaning Companies
metaDescription: Pressure washing marketing from ASP: Google Business Profile, search, Google Ads and Facebook, tracked to booked jobs. Your accounts stay in your name.
intro: ASP is a pressure washing marketing agency for house wash, roof cleaning and flatwork companies. We run your Business Profile, website, Google Ads and Facebook ads as one system and report it against booked jobs and revenue. Everything we build is set up in your name.

sections.heading: How demand works for pressure washing
paragraphs: Federal data doesn't track pressure washing on its own. The trade has no NAICS code of its own; the closest federal category is Other Services to Buildings and Dwellings, which lists building exterior cleaning and drain or gutter cleaning as examples. That same category also includes pool, chimney and duct cleaning.

Employment in the broader category swings with the season: US private employment was 103,283 in January 2024 and 131,517 in July 2024. Those are worker counts, not a measure of customer demand. Pool cleaning sits in the same group, so that swing can't be pinned on pressure washing alone, and that is why we build your marketing calendar from your own booked jobs once tracking is in place.

sections.heading: The channels ASP runs for pressure washing companies
paragraphs: Most of the work starts with Google. According to Google, three things mainly decide local results: relevance, distance and prominence. Google also says no one can pay to rank higher in them. A business that travels to customers without a storefront gets one service-area profile, and Google says the area generally shouldn't extend past about 2 hours' drive from its base, though larger areas can suit some businesses.
Each channel below has a clear role in the plan.
bullets: Google Business Profile: services listed accurately, before-and-after photos, steady review requests and weekly posts.
Website and service pages: house washing, roof cleaning, concrete and flatwork, decks and fences, each answering what a buyer wants to know before calling.
Google Search Ads: the main paid channel, since Google's Local Services Ads list had no pressure washing category when it was checked on October 15, 2026.
Facebook and Instagram: before-and-after video, seasonal offers and retargeting site visitors who didn't book.

sections.heading: Trust signals that belong on your site
paragraphs: Put the credentials your company holds where buyers will see them. The Power Washers of North America, a non-profit trade association founded in 1992, reports issuing more than 7,000 certifications. Its House Wash Certification teaches contractors to clean homes with low-pressure methods, covering chemical handling and surface protection. The United Association of Mobile Contract Cleaners offers certifications including Wash Water Control, Roof Cleaning and Wood Restoration.

How you handle runoff is worth explaining too. In its lead-safe renovation guidance, EPA advises proper disposal of pressure washing waste water and points firms to their local water treatment authority. If your crews capture or route wash water by local rules, a short section on your site says so plainly.

sections.heading: How we measure pressure washing marketing
paragraphs: We report calls, forms, booked jobs and revenue by channel, not clicks alone. Tracking numbers tag each call by source, and forms pass their source into your CRM so it stays attached to the job, where your CRM supports it.

Repeat customers get counted separately. A homeowner who books a house wash every year was won once, so later visits count as retention instead of new acquisition, which keeps each channel's numbers honest. If you run Housecall Pro, ASP is an Official Housecall Pro Affiliate Partner and sets up Housecall Pro attribution as part of the Foundation tier.

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: Your website, domain, Business Profile and reviews, ad accounts, call tracking and CRM data are built in your name. Ad spend goes from your accounts straight to Google and Meta. If you ever leave, there's no exit fee to take it all with you.

faqs.question: What does a pressure washing marketing agency do?
faqs.answer: It runs the channels that turn local searches into booked jobs: your Business Profile, website, Google Ads and Facebook ads, plus the tracking that shows which one produced each job. ASP runs those as one system and reviews them with you every month.

faqs.question: Can pressure washing companies run Google Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Not under a pressure washing category. Google's US list had no pressure washing or power washing category when it was checked on October 15, 2026, and Google describes the list as what's available "at this time," so it can change. Our pressure washing advertising page covers how we build paid search without it.

faqs.question: Do PWNA or UAMCC certifications help my marketing?
faqs.answer: They give buyers a specific reason to trust you. Both are voluntary association certifications, not licenses, so their value comes from showing them clearly. We put them on your site, profile and ads where a homeowner comparing quotes will see them.

faqs.question: How do you plan around slow months?
faqs.answer: We plan budget and content around your calendar rather than a national average, since federal data doesn't track pressure washing on its own. Spend leads into your busy months and pulls back when crews are booked. After a season of tracked jobs, your own numbers set the schedule.

faqs.question: What does pressure washing marketing cost?
faqs.answer: ASP's Foundation tier is $2,500 a month and Growth is $3,850 a month, with paid media management included in Growth. Local SEO Pro runs on its own at $1,200 a month. Ad spend is separate; our pricing page shows what each tier includes.

faqs.question: Who owns my accounts if I leave?
faqs.answer: You do, the whole time. Everything is set up in your name from day one, and ASP charges no exit fees to transfer it. Our what-you-own page lists each asset.
